children: The yield on the U.S. 10-year bond has moved to a fresh post-2007 high of 5.301%. The market price action suggests investors are trading with more of a "sell rallies" than "buy dips" mindset, says ANZ in a note to clients. Caution remains warranted as the bond rout continues and New Zealand rates will be biased higher in the coming session, it adds. Spreads to U.S. bonds are moving further into negative territory, consistent with the better relative fiscal outlook in New Zealand, it adds. That is resulting in local yields rising more slowly rather than bucking the global trend and falling, ANZ says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
